headline: After Nifty's best day in months, a US tech crash overnight points to a lower open. Cheaper oil and record foreign buying should limit the damage.

mood.label: Mixed
mood.why: The dashboard's checks lean positive (score +49, 3 of 4 agree), but the overnight news is clearly bad, so today could go either way. Overnight data as of 08:46 IST.

key_points.text: The US had its worst day since April 2025: S&P 500 **−4.4%**, Nasdaq −5.5%, led by AI and chip stocks. Asia is falling too.
GIFT Nifty (the overnight pointer for India's open) is around 24,410–24,420, about **120–170 points** below Thursday's close of 24,537.
Foreign investors (FIIs) bought **₹14,975 crore** on Thursday, about 4 times normal and the most since September 2024. Cheaper oil (Brent near $99) also helps India.
My call: a dip or pause today is more likely than another big rise, but India should fall less than Asia. Confidence is low.

sections.title: What changed overnight
sections.summary: The night brought worse news for the open, and it works against Thursday's big rise.

points.text: US tech shares fell **7.3%** on worries about AI spending and the US election. US futures are up slightly this morning, so the selling has paused.
Asia this morning: Nikkei −5.3%, Kospi −3.6% after an 8% drop at the open, Taiwan −2.9%. Chip makers Samsung and SK Hynix fell about **10%**.
Indian shares listed in the US rose on the crash day: Infosys +4.6%, ICICI Bank +4.1%. This suggests India is seen as **less exposed** to the AI selloff.

Brent is near **$99.5**, down about 12% this week on hopes of calm in West Asia, though up 1.3% this morning. US bond rates and the dollar barely moved. (The dashboard's 'since India closed' figures use an old 23 Oct snapshot, so I used daily changes.)

sections.title: Bounce or continuation?
sections.summary: After a +2.4% day, I expect a lower open and a pause, not a collapse. Low confidence.

points.text: For a pullback: bad news overnight, Asia falling, six straight up days, and domestic funds (DIIs) sold **₹10,445 crore** on Thursday, likely taking profits.
Open futures positions fell **4.6%** as prices rose: much of the jump was bets on a fall being closed, which fades faster than fresh buying.
For more gains: FIIs bought for a fifth day, their share of futures bets on a rise jumped from 13.6% to **21.6%**, and option sellers are guarding 24,200–24,500.
What would prove me wrong: Nifty recovering above **24,550** with FIIs buying again would mean the rise continues. A fall below 24,200 would mean a deeper drop.

sections.title: The big picture
sections.summary: The dashboard reads the trend as positive, with a score of +49 out of 100.

points.text: Nifty is above its 20, 50 and 200-day averages, but recent highs and lows still form a sideways range. Trend score: **+1.0** out of 2.
Futures and FII positions score **+1.25**; the option chain scores +1.33, as most new activity was bets that Nifty won't fall.
Put-call ratio (bets on a fall compared with bets on a rise) is **1.29**, flat over 5 days: a weak +0.3.
India VIX (expected swings) is 15.6, above 72% of the past year. Options are **expensive**: traders still want protection.

sections.title: What big investors are doing
sections.summary: Foreign investors are buying hard while domestic funds sell into the rise.

points.text: FIIs have bought **₹32,210 crore** so far in November, after selling on most days in October.
DIIs sold **₹18,228 crore** this month. The two big groups are trading against each other.
In late October FIIs bought telecom (₹11,065 crore) and **IT (₹10,915 crore)**, and sold consumer goods, autos and oil firms.

sections.title: What the world is telling India
sections.summary: Cheaper oil helps India, but the global AI crash and US rate worries hurt.

points.text: Cheaper oil eases India's inflation and import bill, since India buys over **85%** of its oil abroad. The rupee also firmed on Thursday.
The US fear gauge (VIX) jumped **70%** to 28. Scared global investors often pull money from emerging markets.
US 6-month bills pay 4.19%, above the Fed's 3.88%, so markets expect a possible Fed **rate rise**. That pulls money back to the US.

sections.title: Company results
sections.summary: No Nifty 50 company reported in the last week; the bigger names were mostly steady.

points.text: Britannia: sales up 15.6%, profit up **10.8%** from last year, in line. I couldn't confirm analysts' forecasts.
Mphasis (IT): sales up 17.4%, profit up **19.6%**, close to 'Strong'. Kalpataru Projects profit rose 23%.
Tata Steel, the next Nifty 50 company to report, is due on 7 November.

sections.title: What could change the picture
sections.summary: A busy few days: US jobs data tonight, a Diwali session on Sunday, and expiry on Monday.

points.text: US jobs report tonight at 19:00 IST (forecast +65,000 jobs). Strong numbers could raise US rate-hike fears.
Muhurat (Diwali) trading on **Sunday 8 November**, reported as 14:20–15:30 IST. India CPI follows on 12 November.
Weekly Nifty options expiry on Monday 9 November: prices can swing near the big levels of 24,000 and 25,000.
If the AI selloff spreads, FIIs may **slow their buying**, removing the main support for this rally.

levels.note: Option sellers guard 25,000 above and 24,000 below. A close above 25,000 would signal a strong new leg up; a close below 24,000 would undo most of Thursday's jump.

watch.text: Size of the gap-down open. A fall of under 0.7% would mean India is holding up better than Asia.
IT shares: do they gain as money leaves AI and chip stocks abroad?
Whether FIIs keep buying in today's provisional data after the close.
US jobs report. A strong number could revive fears of a US rate hike.
Brent crude: staying under $100 keeps the oil support for India in place.

bottom_line: The dashboard leans positive, helped by record foreign buying and cheaper oil. But a global AI-led crash came after India closed, so a lower open looks likely, and my read is a dip or pause rather than a collapse. Confidence is low because overnight news and India's own signals point opposite ways. The main risk is global selling deepening and FIIs turning cautious.
